newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. chief deplores grenade attack in Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief deplores grenade attack in Cambodia.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan on Monday deplored a weekend grenade attack that killed at least 14 people in Cambodia and called on the government to investigate the violence immediately.

The attack during a demonstration of the opposition Khmer National Party in the capital of Phnom Penh was the most blatant act of political violence to hit Cambodia's fragile democracy since the current coalition government came to power after U.N.-organised elections in May 1993.

"The secretary-general deplores the attack against peaceful demonstrators in Phnom Penh on Sunday ... and calls on the Royal Government of Cambodia to investigate this act of violence and take all appropriate measures to see that such incidents are not repeated," spokesman Fred Eckhard said.
"He also calls on all sides to exercise restraint and to do their utmost to ensure a political process conducive to the holding of free and fair elections scheduled for 1997 and 1998," he said.

Protest leader Sam Rainsy, who narrowly escaped injury, has blamed the attack on his bitter foe, co-premier Hun Sen. But an Interior Ministry spokesman said it was unclear who was responsible and an investigation was underway.
